explanation: Copy the digits, then clear trailing nines while carrying one leftward. Increment the first digit below nine; if every digit was nine, insert a leading one.
timeComplexity: O(n): copying n digits is required even when the carry stops immediately; the carry scan and possible leading insertion are also at most linear.
spaceComplexity: O(n+1) for the returned copied digits; O(1) scalar carry state.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: Adding one affects only the suffix through the first digit below nine. Every carried position represents ten units of its place, which is exactly one unit of the place to its left; replacing ten with zero and carrying therefore preserves the value of the desired sum. When the carry stops, all digits are valid and the result is the original number plus one. If it passes the first position, the original number was all nines, so the result is one followed by n zeros.
walkthrough: For [7,9,9], clear the last 9, clear the next 9, then increment 7. The copied digits become [8,0,0].
edgeCases: Input is a nonempty canonical decimal digit sequence; zero is [0].
Without a trailing nine, only the final digit increases.
This implementation returns a copy and leaves the caller’s digits unchanged.
